messages:
Samira Patel: Quick heads-up — ran into three small DX pain points w/ the Go SDK while wiring streaming generators into a sample app. Posting a tiny repro + suggested API ergonomics. cc @Alex Chen :eyes:

Alex Chen: thanks for calling this out. can you paste the repro? is this about cancellation or about how tokens are delivered?

Samira Patel: both. minimal pattern I used:

```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
defer cancel()
client := redwood.NewClient(apiKey)
gen, err := client.NewGenerator(ctx, redwood.GeneratorOptions{Model: "rw-v1"})
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
for gen.Next() {
    tok := gen.Text() // blocks until next token
    fmt.Print(tok)
}
if err := gen.Err(); err != nil { log.Printf("gen err: %v", err) }
```

Samira Patel: Problems I saw: 1) gen.Next() can block even after ctx cancelled (takes ~500ms to bail depending on underlying HTTP timeouts). 2) No obvious way to stream with per-token context (e.g., for per-request timeouts). 3) ergonomics: consumer code ends up juggling gen.Close() + ctx in awkward ways.

Jordan Liu: ouch. that's going to be a common pattern for people hooking up to UIs and websockets. any workaround?

Samira Patel: workaround is to run the iteration in a goroutine and select on ctx.Done(), but that's noisy and leaks if you forget to close. e.g.:

```go
ctx2, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
ch := make(chan string)
go func() {
   defer close(ch)
   for gen.Next() { ch <- gen.Text() }
}()
select {
case <-ctx2.Done(): gen.Close()
case t := <-ch: ...
}
```

Miguel Torres: Yikes. For streaming SDKs I've seen APIs that take the ctx on Next: `Next(ctx)` which lets the call return quickly when ctx is cancelled. Also an io.Reader-style interface can help for raw bytes.

Alex Chen: agree — two concrete options: 1) change `Generator.Next()` -> `Next(ctx context.Context) bool` (backwards compatible if we add a new method) or 2) provide `Stream(ctx)` that returns a receive-only channel of events plus a cancel func. Thoughts on naming and semantics?

Samira Patel: `Next(ctx)` feels nicest for incremental adoption. Example suggested usage:

```go
it, _ := client.NewGenerator(opts)
for it.Next(ctx) {
   token := it.Text()
   fmt.Print(token)
}
if err := it.Err(); err != nil { ... }
```

Samira Patel: also propose adding `Close()` semantics that are documented: Close should abort inflight network requests and unblock Next(ctx). Right now Close exists but doesn't guarantee immediate unblock.

Jordan Liu: we should also document what retry behavior looks like when ctx is cancelled vs when a transient network error happens. SDK currently retries automatically and that interacts badly with per-token timeouts.

Miguel Torres: +1. Recommend explicit per-request retry policy override on the generator options, and that Next(ctx) cancellation should suppress further retries.

Alex Chen: actionable plan: Samira — can you open an RFC that outlines the minimal API changes (Next(ctx), clarify Close semantics, add opt-in Stream channel helper) + a tiny example app that demonstrates per-token cancellation? If we like it we can land it as a minor semver bump.

Samira Patel: will do. I'll add a sample app under examples/go/streaming-context and include a tiny server that proxies tokens to a websocket showing graceful cancellation. I'll also create a backlog ticket for retry semantics.

devex-bot: Created issue RDW-3241: "Go SDK: generator Next(ctx) & streaming cancellation semantics" and linked PR stub.

Alex Chen: perfect. please @ me on the RFC. once we have example code we can ask eng-runtime to validate that Close really aborts the HTTP request.

Samira Patel: will ping. thanks all :thumbsup:
